10.1029/2018JB015511 TheTethyandrifthistoryoftheGondwana-derivedblockstowardstheEurasianlandmasshasbeenahotly
debated topic for decades (Cocks & Torsvik, 2013; Collins, 2003; Ferrari et al., 2008; Metcalfe, 1986, 1996,
Received17JAN2018
1999, 2001, 2002, 2011a, 2011b, 2013; Scotese, 2004; Torsvik & Cocks, 2013). The Indochina (or Annamia)
Accepted18MAY2018
Acceptedarticleonline24MAY2018 BlockisconsideredtobeoneofthemajorblockstoseparatefromeasternGondwanaanddriftnorthward
Publishedonline15JUN2018 andamalgamatewiththeothereasternAsiablocks(e.g.,NorthChinaandTarimblocks)alongthesouthern
marginofEurasiaduringtheMesozoicera.ThelatePaleozoicpaleo-positionanddrifthistoryoftheIndochina
Block has remained one of the biggest unresolved problems in the paleogeographic reconstructions of
easternAsia withintheGondwanaand Pangeasupercontinent assemblies (Cocks& Torsvik,2013;Collins,
2003;Metcalfe,2011a,2011b,2013;Scotese,2004;Torsvik&Cocks,2013).Insomereportedreconstructions,
Indochina is considered to be similar paleobiogeographically with the South China Block, implying a
continentalconnectionbetweenthem;asuper-terraneisthusbelievedtoexistinthePaleo-Tethysduring
the Carboniferous-Permian and termed Cathaysialand (Metcalfe, 2009; Wu et al., 1995). Although little is
known on the Paleozoic position of the Qiangtang blocks, studies on the late Paleozoic sedimentary
sequences and fossils also suggests a Cathaysia-affinity for the North Qiangtang Block (Jin, 2002; Zhang
et al., 2009). The widely referred but yet to be confirmed Cathaysianland model is primarily attributed to
tectonostratigraphicand paleontological evidencesfrom thePaleozoic to Mesozoicrocks (Metcalfe,2001,
2011a,2013),althoughconflictinginterpretationsarealsoacknowledged(Fang&Cope,2004).
PreviouspaleomagneticworkonPaleozoicrocksoftheIndochinaBlockhasbeencarriedoutintheLoei-Nam
Nao area of eastern Thailand by Chen and Courtillot (1989) and Yang and Besse (1993), in northwestern
Thailand by Bhongsuwan and Elming (2000), and in southern Peninsular Thailand by Bhongsuwan and
Elming(2000)andRichterandFuller(1996).Allofthesestudiesresolvedmagnetizationsthatwereeither
ofsyn-foldingorotherwiseofoverprintedorigin.Theimplicationisthatthefirsthalfofthejourneyofthe

southerlylatitude(Cocks&Torsvik,2013;Scotese,2004;Torsvik&Cocks,2013;Ueno,2003).

2. Geologic Settings andSampling
TheIndochinaBlockisoneofthelargestblocksineasternAsiaandoccupiesmostoftheSoutheastAsia;ithas
formerlybeennamedtheIndosinianCraton(Bunopas&Vella,1978)althoughthenatureofmuchofthecon-
tinentalfoundationremainsunclear.ItsboundarywiththewesternSibumasuBlockwasonceregardedasthe
Nan-Uttaraditlineament(Barr&Macdonald,1987;Bunopas,1981),untiltheSukhothaiTerranebetweenthe
Nan-UttaraditsutureandChianglai-Chiangmaisuturewasrecognizedasanarc-relatedterranedistinctfrom
theremainderofIndochina(Barr&Macdonald,1991).TheNan-UttaraditSuturesubsequentlylostitsstatusas
theclosedremnantofthemainPaleo-TethysOceanandisnowincreasinglyacceptedasaback-arcbasin.The
boundariesbetweenIndochinaandtheotherblocks(e.g.,SongMasutureto SouthChina,Bentong-Raub
suturetoEastMalaya,MedianSumatrasuturetoWestSumatra)havebecomebasicallyclearfollowingthe
workofUeno(2003),SoneandMetcalfe(2008),andUenoetal.(2012),althoughacontrastingassessment
hasbeengivenbyCaiandZhang(2009).
The study area, petrographically the Khao Khwang Platform, geotectonically is the western margin of the
IndochinaBlock.ItcomprisestheareatotheeastoftheNan-UttaraditSutureZone,northofMaePingFault,
andwestoftheNamDukBasin(Figure1;Riddetal.,2011).ThePermiansuccessionintheSaraburiareacom-
prisestheSaraburiGroupandincorporatestheSapBon,KhaoKhad,PangAsok,NongPong,KhaoKhwang,
andPhuPheformations.IntheNakhonSawan-PhetchahunareathePermiansuccessioncomprisestheTak
FaFormation(Figure2).NotethattheseformationsarenearlycontemporaneousasshowninFigureS1in
thesupportinginformation,ratherthaninacontinuoussuccession(Riddetal.,2011).Atotalof280coresin
limestone facies were drilled from 27 sites through five sections using a portable gasoline-powered and
water-cooledhand-drill.Fieldsampleswereorientedusingamagneticcompass,orbothmagneticandsun
compasseswhenfeasible.Bothorientationmethodswereappliedto36%ofthesamplesandidentifiedlocal
geomagneticdeclinationsof(cid:1)1°intheNakhonSawan-Phetchahunareaand(cid:1)2°intheSaraburiarea.
TheTakFaFormationismainlymassivetowell-beddedlimestonewithsubordinatesandstoneandshale,
which stretches from north of Lopburi Province, through the type area at Tak Fa village in southeast
Nakhon Sawan Province northeastwards to Phetchabun Province (Figure 2; Figure S2a; Ridd et al., 2011).
Threesites(Th218,Th219,andTh220)werecollectedfromsection1(roadcut)locatedsoutheastofTakFa
village, and four sites (Th221, Th222, Th223, and Th224) and fivesites (The225,The226, Th227, Th228, and
Th229)wererespectivelycollectedfromsection2(naturalsection)andsection3(quarrysection;FigureS2b)
atthenorthwestofBangSamPhanvillage.TheageofthesethreesectionsoftheTakFaFormationispaleon-
tologicallyconstrainedtothelateEarlyPermiantoearlyMiddlePermian(Chitnarinetal.,2012;Metcalfe&
Sone, 2008), while the Khao Khwang and Nong Pong formations in the Saraburi area are Early-Middle
Permian (Cisuralian-Guadalupian) in age (Fontaine, 2002; Ridd et al., 2011; Udchachon et al., 2014). The
Khao Khwang Formation is dark to light gray, thick bedded limestone with nodular chert (Figure S2c
andS2d),whichoccursinthenorthernpartoftheSaraburiarea,andtheNongPongFormationislaminated
tothinorthickbeddedshaleandthinbeddedlimestoneswithlocallydevelopedchert,distributedwidelyin
thecentralpartoftheSaraburiarea(Figure2;Riddetal.,2011).SitesTh392-402andTh403-406werecol-
lectedfromsection4(roadcut)oftheKhaoKhwangFormationandsection5(roadcut)oftheNongPong
Formation,respectively(Figure2).
ThePermianstrataareseparatedfromtheMesozoicsedimentsbytheIndosinianIUnconformity,whichwas
formedduringthemostintenseepisodeoftheIndosinianOrogenyandcorrespondedtothegreatUpper
Permian to Middle Triassic hiatus. Most Paleozoic strata were deformed or folded during the Indosinian I
Event,althoughitsactualtimingcannotbecloselyconstrained(Riddetal.,2011).

3. Paleomagnetic Analysis
3.1. LaboratoryMethods
In the laboratory, the core samples, generally 2.5 cm in diameter and 6–13 cm in length, were trimmed
into standard cylindrical specimens; ~2.2 cm in length with long samples were cut into two specimens
designated S (inner) and S (outer). Systematic rock magnetic analyses were conducted on samples
i o
powdered from representative fresh end material to identify the dominant magnetic carriers. Acquisition
and back-field demagnetization of IRM (isothermal remanent magnetization) and hysteresis loops were
measured with a Micro 3900 vibrating sample magnetometer (3900VSM) at room temperature with an
applied field range of ±1.0 or ±1.5 T. For samples not saturated at up to 1.5 T, acquisition of IRM at up
to2.7TwasmeasuredoncylindricalspecimenS (whilespecimenS cutfromthesamesamplereserved
o i
for paleomagnetic measurement) using a 2G-755R cryogenic magnetometer and 2G Enterprises pulse
magnetizer. Temperature dependence of the magnetic susceptibility was determined in argon from

roomtemperatureto700°CusinganAGICOmultifunctionKappabridge(MFK1).Representativecylindrical
S specimens were used for three-axis IRMs (Lowrie, 1990) and magnetized with 0.1, 0.5, and 2.5 T along
o
the X, Y, and Z axes respectively using a 2G Enterprises pulse magnetizer and then thermally
demagnetized using an TD-48 demagnetization oven and measured with a 2G-755R cryogenic
magnetometer. In addition, low temperature measurement of IRM was made in the range of 15–300 K
to identify the diagnostic Verwey transition for magnetite, the Morin transition for hematite, and the
34 K transition for pyrrhotite, using a Magnetic Property Measurement System-Extra Large 5
Superconducting Quantum Interference Device (MPMS-XL5SQUID). Samples were first cooled from 300
to 15 K in zero field (ZFC), followed by applying a 2.5 T field at 15 K, and measured from 15 to 300 K.
The cooling-warming cycle of a saturation isothermal remnant magnetization (SIRM) imparted at 300 K
with 2.5 T was measured in a zero-magnetic field.
Following rock magnetic analyses and the measurements of natural remanent magnetization, specimens
were subjected to low temperature thermal cycles in liquid nitrogen for two or three times as suggested
byKirschvinketal.(2015)withtheaimoferasingviscouscomponents,whichmightbecarriedbymultido-
main magnetite. Thermal or AF (alternating field) demagnetization was then applied to samples using a
2G-RAPID cryogenic magnetometer in the Paleomagnetism and Geochronology Laboratory (PGL) of the
InstituteofGeologyandGeophysics,ChineseAcademyofSciences.Themagnetometerisinstalledinamag-
netically shielded room with a background field weaker than 300 nT. Thermal demagnetization was con-
ductedusingaPGL-designedTD-PGL-100oven withinternalresidual magneticfieldlowered to lessthan
5nT(generally1–2nT).
Themethodsofprinciplecomponentanalysis(PCA;Kirschvink,1980)orgreat-circlefitting(GC;McFadden&
McElhinny,1988)wereusedinthecalculationofdemagnetizationresults,andFisherstatistics(Fisher,1953)
wereusedinthemeandirectioncalculation.

3.2. RockMagneticResults
Differentmagneticbehaviorsofsamplesfromthethreeformationscanprovideimportantinformationon
thecompositionsofthedominantmagneticminerals.
FortheTakFaFormationsamples,theIRMsaturatedbefore0.2T(Figures3e–3g)andthehysteresisloop
closesbefore0.2T(Figures3band3c)indicatingarelativelylowcoercivity(oranadmixturewithparamag-
netic components like sample Figure 3a) less than 50 mT and centralizes at ~20 mT. Combined with the
recordoftheVerweytransition(Muxworthy&McClelland,2000;Özdemiretal.,2002;Verwey,1939)identified
in the ZFC (Figure 3h), the dominant magnetic carrier in the Tak Fa Formation samples is interpreted to
bemagnetite.
The Khao Khwang Formation samples have a dominant soft component (less than 0.1 T) after the hard
component (0.5–2.5 T) is erased before 100°C (Figure 3j), which decreases toward zero after 500°C
(Figure3k).ThedifferentialofIRMsindicateaveryhighcoercivitycomponentandacomponentwithlow
coercivity less than 50 mT showing a tendency to saturation before 1.0 T (Figure 3i). Together with the
unblocking temperature at ~580°C (Figure 3l), the dominant magnetic minerals in the Khao Khwang
Formationsamplesappeartobeamixtureofmagnetiteandgoethite.Thisinterpretationisalsoconfirmed
inthesubsequentthermaldemagnetizations,whichrevealsasharpdropbefore120°Candastablecompo-
nentabovethistemperature(Figures4e–4g).
FortheNongPongFormationsamples,theIRMsaturatesafter1.5T,whosedifferentialrevealstwopartially
overlappingcoercivitycomponentscenteredatlessthan100and~200 mT,respectively(Figure 3m).The
thermaldemagnetizationofthethree-axisIRMshowsthatthesoftcomponent(lessthan0.1T)decreases
towardzeroafter500°C,afterthemediumcomponent(0.1–0.5T)hasdroppedsharplybetween300–350°C
(Figure3q).AssociatedwiththeVerweytransitionand~34Ktransition(Dekkersetal.,1989;Rochetteetal.,
1990;Wolfersetal.,2011)identifiedinRT-SIRM(Figures3nand3p)andZFC(Figures3rand3t),finegrain
magnetite and pyrrhotite are identified to be the dominant magnetic carriers in the Nong Pong
Formationsamples.
3.3. PaleomagneticResults
3.3.1. TakFaFormation
Onehundredtwenty-threefieldsamplesfrom12siteswerecollectedfromtheTakFaFormation,andtwo
groups of characteristic remanent magnetizations (ChRMs) denoted Groups 1 and 2 were isolated. In
Group1onlyonecomponentcanbeisolatedduringtheAFdemagnetizationupto110mT(Figure4b)with
thedirectionsofsamplesfromsitesTh220,Th221,Th222,Th223,andTh224clusteringinthelocationofthe
presentgeomagneticfieldanddispersingfollowingtiltadjustment(FigureS1andTableS1).Hence,Group1
isinterpretedtobeanoverprintinthepresentgeomagneticfield(FigureS1a).Group2comprisesfoursites,
including one with reversed polarity (Th219) and three with normal polarity (Th226, Th228, and Th229;
Figure 5a). Two contrasting component directions were isolated from these samples (Figures 4a, 4c, and
4d)withthehighfieldcomponent(>20mT)interpretedastheChRM.
3.3.2. KhaoKhwangFormation
Onehundredfourteensamplesfrom11siteswerecollectedfromtheKhaoKhwangFormation.Followinga
sharpdropofthemagnetizationbetweennaturalremanentmagnetizationand150°Cprobablycorrespond-
ingtothepresenceofgoethite,thelowtemperaturecomponentwaserasedbefore~350°C,andthestable
component was isolated between ~350 and 520°C or higher and interpreted as the ChRM. Note that the
magnetizationhaddroppedtoseveral10
(cid:1)6A/m(correspondingtothemagneticmomentofstandardspeci-
mensin10
(cid:1)8emu)afterremovalofthelowtemperaturecomponent(Figures4e,4f,and4g).Isolationofthe
veryweakbutstablehightemperaturecomponentbenefitedfromtheoptimized2G-RAPIDmagnetometer
and especially thegood performanceof theTD-PGL-100 oven.As a result, ChRMs couldbe isolated from
sevensitesinthisformationinsection4(normalpolarity:Th392,Th394,Th397,Th398,Th401,andTh402;
reversalpolarity:Th395;Figure5b).

McFadden’s(1990)foldtest(insituξ =12.252,tilt-correctedξ =2.984,ξ criticalvalue=4.510and6.305

at 95% and 99% confidence level for N = 15) with an optimal clustering at 88.4 ± 5.4% before and

test(McFadden&McElhinny,1990)withr=13.5°>r_critical=11.0°.Thiscouldbeduetoregionalrelative
rotationbetweenthesesectionswiththesamecausepossiblycontributingtothedeviationoftheoptimal

ChRMsofallthe15sitesfromthethreeformationsinthecalculationofmeanresult,sincethattheagesof
thethreeformationsareoverlappedpartiallytoeachother,asawhole,theEarly-MiddlePermian.

4.1. IsthePyrrhotiteRecordReliable?
Thepresenceofpyrrhotite(Fe S )isincreasinglybeingreportedfromsediments,althoughgeochemicalcon-

ditionsrequiredfortheformationofpyrrhotitearepoorlyunderstoodandmanyfactorsareconsideredto
potentiallycontributetotheformationofferromagneticironsulfides(greigiteandpyrrhotite).Theseinclude
theavailabilityoffineiron-containingmineralandsulfategrains,bioactivityandspecificredoxconditions.It
canbeauthigenicproductsfromanearlystageofdiagenesisunderanoxicsedimentaryenvironments(Hall&
Evans, 1995; Kao et al., 2004). It may also occur in a late stage of lithification as a record of syn-folding

magnetization(Kars&Kodama,2015;Weaveretal.,2002)whileinsomespecificconditionsitalsomaybe
detritalinorigin(Horngetal.,1998;Horng&Roberts,2006).
Inthisstudy,wetendtointerpretthepyrrhotiteasofdetritaloriginfortworeasons.First,magnetiteandpyr-
rhotitecoexistinthelimestonesamples andrecordthesamemagnetizationcomponents asdiscussedin
section3.3.3,whichstronglyindicatethattheChRMsarereliable.
4.2. ThePaleo-PositionsoftheIndochinaBlock
TheFisherianmean(Fisher,1953)ofthevirtualgeomagneticpolesoftheTakFaandKhaoKhwangforma-
tionsyieldsapaleomagneticpoleat31.9°N,336.9°E(K=69.1,A =5.5°),whichisnotsignificantlydifferent
95
fromthatforallthethreeformationsat34.1°N,331.7°E(K=45.4,A =5.7°;Table1).Althoughtheformerpole
95
resultedfromadatasetwithmorerobustfieldtest(section4.2),weinclinetousethelateroneasthepaleo-
magneticpoleinthetectonicanalysesdiscussedbelowbecauseinclusionofthedatafromtheNongPong
FormationcanpotentiallybemorerepresentativeoftheEarly-MiddlePermianagerange.
Theelongation-inclinationmethoddevelopedbyTauxeandKent(2004)wasusedtoestimatethelikelyincli-
nationshallowingerroron105sampleswhosedirectionswerecalculatedwithPCA(Kirschvink,1980).Ashal-
lowing factor of f = 0.8 is produced after 1,000 bootstrap simulations (Figures 6i and 6j), which gives a
correctedinclinationof45.6°with95%confidencelimitsbetween39.4°and52.9°.Thefactor(f=0.8)isused
forthecorrectionofthedatasetincluding105PCA-calculatedand12GC-calculatedsamples.Thepolewas
correctedfrom34.1°N,331.7°E(K=45.4,A =5.7°)to31.2°N,327.3°E(K=45.4,A =5.7°;Figure6)andcor-
95 95
respondstoapaleolatitudecorrectionfrom21.2±5.7°Sto25.9±5.7°Satthecenterofstudyarea(15°N,
101°E),or10.9±5.7°Sto15.6±5.7°Satthereferencesite(28°N,100°E).Theinclinationshallowingeffectis
supposedtobenotsignificantinthisstudyontheconsiderationofthepaleolatitudecorrectionof~4.7°rela-
tivetotheuncertaintyof5.7°.WetendtobeconservativeinusingtheindistinctivelyE-Icorrectedresultfor
thepotentialriskthattheelongationisresultedfromprobablerelativerotationbetweendifferentsections.
Thus,theEarly-MiddleIndochinaBlockisinterpretedtobelocatedatamiddle-lowlatitude(21.2±5.7°S)posi-
tionintheSouthernHemisphere(Figures7and8a)consistentwiththetropicalrestorations(Cocks&Torsvik,
2013;Scotese,2004;Torsvik&Cocks,2013;Ueno,2003)butcontrastingwiththeequatorialmodel(Collins,
2003; Ferrari et al., 2008; Metcalfe, 1996, 1999, 2001, 2002, 2011a, 2011b, 2013). This suggests that the
Indochina Block had drifted away from the northern margin of Gondwana by the Early-Middle Permian
(ca.280Ma;Figures7and8a),followedbya~5,000-km(~47°oflatitudinaldifference)northwardtransition
untilitmergedtothesouthernmarginoftheEurasianregionintheIndosinianOrogenyEventbytheNorian
StageoftheLateTriassic(ca.220Ma;Figures7and8b;Yanetal.,2017).Thisimpliesanaveragenorthward
driftrateof~9cm/yearrelativetotheEarth’srotationaxis,and~4.5cm/yearrelativetoGondwana,because
Gondwanahadmovednorthwardby~23°duringthesametimeinterval(ca.280Matoca.220Ma;Torsvik
et al., 2012). The estimation of ~4.5 cm/year is a cumulative result of the closing of the Paleo-Tethys and
theopeningoftheNeo-Tethys(Lietal.,2016;Scotese,2004).
4.3. ThePaleogeographicConfigurationandDriftingHistoryoftheCathaysialand
Indochina was identified paleontologically to be of Cathaysia/Tethys affinity during the Carboniferous to
TriassicorevenEarlyJurassic(Metcalfe,2011a).ThetypicalCathaysianGiagantopterisfloraswererecognized
intheIndochinaBlockaswellasintheSouthChinaandNorthChinablocks,andtheendemicoccurrenceof
PseudosweetognathusontheIndochinaandSouthChinablockswasconsideredtobeanevidencefortheir
continentalconnectionorcloseaffinity(Metcalfe&Sone,2008).Therecognitionofophiolite,high-pressure
metamorphicrocks(eclogiteandblueschist)fromcentralQiangtang(Kappetal.,2000,2003;Zhaietal.,2007,
2009,2011;Zhangetal.,2006)suggeststheLongmucuo-ShuanghuSuturebetweentheNorthQiangtang
andSouthQiangtangblocksmaybethewestwardextensionoftheChangning-MenglianSutureandrepre-
sentsthemainsuturezoneofthePaleo-TethysOcean(Metcalfe,2013;Zhaietal.,2011).Paleomagneticdata
isolatedfromLateCarboniferoustoEarlyPermiansedimentaryrocks(Yangetal.,2017)andEarlyPermian
(296.9 ± 1.9 Ma) volcanic rocks (Song et al., 2017) indicated similar paleolatitudinal position (30–34°S;
Figure7andTableS2)fortheNorthQiangtangBlock,whichisingoodagreementwiththepaleo-position
oftheSouthChinaBlockassynthesizedbyCocksandTorsvik(2013).Notethatthesynthesizedapparent
polarwanderpathsoftheSouthChinaBlockinCocksandTorsvik(2013)shouldbeusedcautiouslybecause
inclinationcorrectionwithafactorof0.6toallclasticsedimentaryrocksandmayleadtoanunnecessary

5. Conclusions
We provide a new high-quality Early-Middle paleomagnetic pole from central Thailand for the Indochina
Block,whichindicatesapaleolatitudeof21.2±5.7°Sforthecenterofstudyarea(15°N,101°E).Thetropical
patternratherthantheequatorialpatternoflatePaleozoicrestorationofIndochinaissupported.Weconfirm
that the Indochina Block had drifted away from the northern margin of Gondwana by the Early-Middle
Permian.TheaveragerateoftheIndochinaBlockdriftingawayfromGondwanaisestimatedas~4.5cm/year
andaconcurrentdriftinghistoryissupposedfortheIndochina,NorthQiangtang,andSouthChinablocks.
The model of Cathaysialand including the South China, Indochina, and North Qiangtang blocks is
quantitativelysupported.
